ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: I looked at the attached figure: this is a square, with a diagonal drawn from the upper-left corner to the lower-right corner. This diagonal is divided by four points into five segments, labeled in order as a, b, c, d, e. The figure also draws line segments from these points to the vertices of the square, forming several triangles; the marked areas are respectively the top triangle 2 cm^2, the left triangle 5 cm^2, the right triangle 9 cm^2, and the bottom triangle 4 cm^2. Reasoning: According to the method, let the four corners of the square be TL, TR, BR, BL, and the diagonal goes from TL to BR. Let the four division points in order be P1, P2, P3, P4, where a=TL to P1, b=P1 to P2, c=P2 to P3, d=P3 to P4, e=P4 to BR. Let the side length of the square be S, then S^2=30, so when any side is taken as the base, the triangle area coefficient is S^2/2=15. Let ti be the diagonal proportion from TL to Pi. From the areas in the figure: the area of triangle TL-TR-P1 is 2, so 2=15t1, giving t1=2/15. The area of triangle TL-BL-P2 is 5, so 5=15t2, giving t2=5/15. The area of triangle TR-BR-P3 is 9, so 9=15(1-t3), giving t3=6/15. The area of triangle BL-BR-P4 is 4, so 4=15(1-t4), giving t4=11/15. Therefore the proportions of the five segments on the whole diagonal in order are: a=t1=2/15, b=t2-t1=3/15, c=t3-t2=1/15, d=t4-t3=5/15, e=1-t4=4/15. The largest is d.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and cumulative fractions along the diagonal. From the image, label the square corners TL, TR, BR, BL and let the diagonal run TL to BR through segments a,b,c,d,e. Let P1, P2, P3, P4 be the four marked interior points, so P1 follows segment a, P2 follows b, P3 follows c, and P4 follows d. Put the square side length S, so S^2=30. If ti is the fraction of the diagonal from TL to Pi, then the areas read from the image give: triangle TL-TR-P1 has area 2, triangle TL-BL-P2 has area 5, triangle TR-BR-P3 has area 9, and triangle BL-BR-P4 has area 4. Each such triangle has base S and height equal to S times either ti or 1-ti. Since S^2/2=15, solve 2=15t1, 5=15t2, 9=15(1-t3), 4=15(1-t4). This gives t1=2/15, t2=5/15, t3=6/15, t4=11/15. Therefore the diagonal segment fractions are a=2/15, b=3/15, c=1/15, d=5/15, e=4/15 of the whole diagonal, so the longest is d.
